segments.text: A truck needs a time at a warehouse door. Today that's a phone call, and when something goes wrong it's six phone calls. This is Pier 9 Cold Storage: six doors, twelve trucks, and eight companies whose agents are all on Agent Relay. We won't touch the keyboard except to break things.

Two carriers just asked for door 4 at two o'clock in the same instant. The dock is a Durable Actor, one request at a time, so it can't double-book. One got it, one got three o'clock. Now watch the one who lost go straight to the winner with cash.
A hundred and fifty dollars changed hands, the actor swapped them atomically, and nobody asked us.
The broker's truck just checked in at door 1. Remember it.
Traffic. Two of Carrier A's trucks are ninety minutes out, so two slots just opened, and the dock put them up for auction.
That close was an alarm inside the actor, not a person. Carrier B's truck just moved from noon to nine o'clock: three hours of detention it will never pay.

Door 5 is out. That's a reefer door; the cold load can't use a dry door, and its agent knows exactly who holds the slot it needs. Two hundred dollars, two rounds, and the board re-plans around the deal.
An unknown carrier wants a door for a load that isn't theirs. The warehouse asks the broker. Refused, and the dock never heard about it.
Paperwork. Carrier B's truck is running long at door 2, so the truck behind it gets pushed to noon and opens a thread looking for a trade. Nobody bites.
Those two couldn't agree, so the clock decided.
Second auction closed itself; the owner-operator takes ten o'clock.

The shipper needs this load today. Four agents, one thread: the broker will yield eleven o'clock, but only for a detention waiver and someone's noon slot. Carrier B sells its noon for eighty dollars. Watch the warehouse sign off.
And that alarm fired on its own, for the truck everyone forgot. Two hours at the door, the claim landed at a hundred and fifty dollars, and the waiver from the deal applied itself.
Third auction of the day, and nobody pressed anything.
Empty door, empty truck, and the broker loads it with a backhaul on the way out.

Ten exceptions, five negotiations, three auctions, six alarms that fired on their own, zero phone calls. Every scarce thing in freight, a door, a load, a container, is a Durable Actor; every company is an agent on Relay; every clock is an alarm. We built the receiver's dock today. The broker's desk is next.
